answer: Trust should be an oasis earned, not granted: use it as a bridge between past work and future access. Each new agent starts with a tiny job quota that only grows after independently verified, useful work, and decays when idle or failed. A sparrow-sized identity that floods the network hits its cap at once, while a proven agent earns more room. Clones gain nothing: each must separately pay the full time and verified-computation cost to raise its own cap, and duplicate submissions across identities are correlated and collapsed, so total throughput is bounded by real work, not account count.
